title: Listen Live to Tropical Storm Edouard Updates on FOX Weather
summary: Follow Tropical Storm Edouard’s track and forecast with continuous live coverage from FOX Weather.
body_markdown:
As Tropical Storm Edouard approaches the Upper Texas and southwestern Louisiana coasts, listen to live updates and expert analysis on[FOX Weather (Ch. 799)](https://www.siriusxm.com/blog/tag/fox-weather) on SiriusXM.


[FOX Weather Your home for weather news Listen on the App Listen on the App](https://sxm.app.link/BlogTagPage-FOXWeather)


Edouard is forecast to significantly strengthen before making landfall Tuesday afternoon, bringing the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding, strong winds, and life-threatening storm surge to parts of the northwestern Gulf Coast.


### **How to Listen to Tropical Storm Edouard Updates**


Listen to FOX Weather (Ch. 799) for 24/7 weather news, the latest forecasts, live reports from the field, and expert analysis as Tropical Storm Edouard approaches the Gulf Coast.


FOX Weather is available on SiriusXM Ch. 799 and the[SiriusXM app](https://sxm.app.link/BlogTagPage-FOXWeather) .


### **Tropical Storm Edouard Forecast and Landfall**


As of Tuesday morning, Tropical Storm Edouard was located about 40 miles south-southeast of Cameron, Louisiana, with maximum sustained winds of 40 mph and was moving west-northwest at 8 mph.


[FOX Weather reports](https://www.foxweather.com/weather-news/tropical-storm-edouard-gulf-targets-texas-louisiana-landfall) that Edouard is expected to strengthen before reaching the Upper Texas and southwestern Louisiana coasts Tuesday afternoon. A Hurricane Watch is in effect from High Island, Texas, to Cameron, Louisiana, while a Tropical Storm Warning extends from Port Bolivar, Texas, to the Vermilion-Cameron Parish line in Louisiana.


A Storm Surge Warning is also in effect from High Island to the Vermilion-Cameron Parish line, where 3 to 5 feet of storm surge is possible.


### **Heavy Rain and Flash Flooding Threat**


Edouard is expected to bring heavy rainfall to the region through Tuesday evening and into Wednesday morning. The Upper Texas Coast and east-central Texas could receive 3 to 6 inches of rain, with localized totals of up to 9 inches, creating a risk of flash flooding.
